mainTopic: Sales and pledges of land that may hide a loan with interest, including uncertain רבית and רבי יהודה's view
overview: The גמרא first gives the final הלכה on three earlier opinions: רב חמא, רבי אלעזר and רבי ינאי. A new משנה follows with two cases. In the first, a field is sold for part of the price, with the rest to be paid whenever the buyer wants, and this is forbidden. In the second, a loan is given against a field with a three-year deadline, and this works. The גמרא asks who eats the field's produce before full payment. רב הונא and רב ענן turn out not to argue, because each is talking about a different wording of the sale. רבא then explains רב ספרא's ברייתא of four outcomes by tying each one to a specific wording. Next come several rulings that forbid deals that only might turn into רבית: a fixed-price promise on a pledged field, and a buy-back condition set by the seller. Each time, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says these rulings are not like רבי יהודה, who permits uncertain רבית. The amud ends with a story about a seller who promised to repay a worried buyer, and אמימר's ruling on that promise continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The final rulings on three earlier opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב חמא, like רבי אלעזר, and like רבי ינאי, who said it makes no difference whether the produce itself or its value is used.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows רב חמא, the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר, and the הלכה follows רבי ינאי, who said: what difference is it to me whether it is the items themselves or their value?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion by stating the final הלכה on three opinions it discussed before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name points back to an earlier case. רב חמא's arrangement is permitted. רבי אלעזר holds that fixed interest (רבית קצוצה) can be taken back through בית דין. רבי ינאי holds that paying a debt with goods or with their money value is treated the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law, the final ruling
Their value or price in money
What difference does it make to me

steps.whatToRemember: The earlier section ends with three rulings: like רב חמא, like רבי אלעזר, and like רבי ינאי (items and their money value are treated the same).

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Rav Chama,
and the halacha is like Rabbi Elazar,
and the halacha is like Rabbi Yannai,
who said: What difference is it to me whether it is them (the items)
or what difference is it to me whether it is their value?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous daf section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב חמא, רבי אלעזר, and רבי ינאי.

steps.title: Selling a field for partial payment with an open-ended deal
steps.stepSummary: If someone sells a field, receives only part of the money, and tells the buyer to bring the rest whenever he wants and then take the field, this is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sold him the field, and the buyer gave him part of the money, and the seller said: 'Whenever you want, bring the money and take what is yours,' it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a sale where only part of the price is paid and the rest is left open-ended, and it rules that this is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until the full payment arrives, it is unclear whose field it really is. That means someone eating the produce in the meantime might be eating something like interest. The משנה does not say who is affected, and the גמרא will ask exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
Part of the price
Money, coins
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה says 'forbidden' but does not say who is forbidden to do what. Do not assume the sale itself is invalid; the גמרא next asks who may eat the produce.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
If he sold him the field,
and the buyer gave him part of the money,
and the seller said to him: Whenever you want,
bring the money and take what is yours –
phrases.notes: 'What is yours' means the field you bought.

phrases.english: it is forbidden.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sale with partial payment where the buyer may complete it whenever he wishes is forbidden, because of רבית concerns.

steps.title: A loan against a field with a three-year deadline
steps.stepSummary: If someone lends money against a field and says that if the loan is not repaid within three years the field is his, then the field becomes his. ביתוס בן זונין did this with the approval of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he lent him money on his field and said to him: 'If you do not pay me from now until three years, it is mine,' then it is his. And this is what ביתוס בן זונין would do, with the approval of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second case, a loan secured by a field with a deadline. It rules that this deal works, and it supports this with what ביתוס בן זונין used to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is set against the first case. Here the deal is clearly a loan, with a set time after which the field passes to the lender. The משנה presents it as permitted, and the story of ביתוס בן זונין shows that the חכמים approved it.

keyTerms.meaning: He lent him money
His field
A man who lent money this way
With the approval or guidance of the Sages

steps.whatToRemember: There are two cases in the משנה. An open-ended partial sale is forbidden. A loan against a field with a fixed three-year deadline works.

phrases.english: If he lent him money on his field,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: אִם אִי אַתָּה נוֹתֵן לִי
phrases.english: and said to him: If you do not give me the money
from now until three years –
it (the field) is mine,
then it is his.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's ruling: once the three years pass without payment, the field belongs to the lender.

phrases.english: And this is what Baitos ben Zunin
would do, with the approval of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second case of the same משנה, set against the first
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loan with a field as security and a three-year deadline works: if unpaid, the field becomes the lender's.

steps.title: Who eats the produce in the meantime?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks, about the first case of the משנה, who is entitled to eat the produce of the field before the full payment arrives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking a clarifying question about the first case. This question sets up the opinions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'forbidden' without explaining who is forbidden. Since the field's ownership is unclear until full payment, the גמרא needs to know who may enjoy the produce during that time.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Produce or profits of the field

phrases.english: GEMARA
Who eats the produce?
phrases.notes: This means during the time before the buyer has paid the rest of the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the משנה's first case means in practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who may enjoy the field's produce while only part of the price has been paid.

steps.title: רב הונא and רב ענן give two answers
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the seller eats the produce. רב ענן says the produce is set aside with a third party.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The seller eats the produce. רב ענן said: The produce is placed with a third party.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question, and their answers seem to disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא treats the field as still belonging to the seller, so the seller eats the produce. רב ענן says nobody eats it yet, and it is held by a third person until it becomes clear who the owner is.

keyTerms.meaning: Seller
They put it in the hands of a third person (from שָׁלֹשׁ, three)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The seller eats the produce.
Rav Anan said:
They place the produce with a third party.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: מוֹכֵר אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא: the seller eats. רב ענן: the produce is held by a third party.

steps.title: They do not really argue: two different deals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב הונא is talking about a deal of 'acquire when you bring the money,' and רב ענן is talking about 'acquire from now once you bring the money.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree. This one is where he said: 'When you bring the money, acquire.' That one is where he said: 'When you bring the money, acquire from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two opinions are not a real argument. Each one is describing a different way the seller worded the deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller said 'acquire when you bring,' the field stays the seller's until full payment, so the seller eats the produce (רב הונא). If he said 'acquire from now,' then once the buyer pays, the field turns out to have been his all along; but if he never pays, it was the seller's. Since we cannot know yet, the produce is held by a third party (רב ענן).

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree
When you bring the money
Acquire it
From now, starting from this moment

steps.whatToRemember: Who eats the produce depends on the wording. 'Acquire when you bring' means the seller eats. 'Acquire from now' means the produce is held by a third party.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Acquire from now' does not mean the buyer owns the field right away no matter what. It only takes effect from now if he later brings the rest of the money.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree.
This one is where he said: When you bring the money, acquire.
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא's case: the field is not the buyer's until he pays, so the seller eats the produce.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר: לְכִי מַיְיתֵית קְנִי מֵעַכְשָׁיו.
phrases.english: That one is where he said: When you bring the money, acquire from now.
phrases.notes: This is רב ענן's case: ownership is unclear until he pays, so the produce is held by a third party.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent disagreement between רב הונא and רב ענן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each opinion fits a different wording of the deal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like רב הונא and רב ענן argue about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each one is talking about a different wording, 'acquire when you bring' versus 'acquire from now,' so there is no argument.

steps.title: רב ספרא's four possible outcomes
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא taught a ברייתא from the school of רבי חייא: sometimes both parties may eat the produce, sometimes neither may, sometimes only the seller may, and sometimes only the buyer may.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא taught in the laws of רבית from the school of רבי חייא: Sometimes both are permitted, sometimes both are forbidden, sometimes the seller is permitted and the buyer forbidden, and sometimes the buyer is permitted and the seller forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists four possible outcomes for who may eat the produce. This sets up the next discussion, where the גמרא will explain which case fits each outcome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists every combination: both allowed, both forbidden, only the seller, or only the buyer. It does not yet explain the cases. It only gives the outline that the גמרא will fill in next.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the study house of רבי חייא
Sometimes
Buyer
Permitted

phrases.english: Rav Safra taught, regarding interest,
from the school of Rabbi Chiya:
Sometimes both of them are permitted,
phrases.notes: Permitted to eat the produce of the field.

phrases.english: sometimes both of them are forbidden,
and sometimes the seller is permitted
and the buyer is forbidden,
and sometimes the buyer is permitted
and the seller is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב סָפְרָא בְּרִבִּית דְּבֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that widens the question of who may eat the produce
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four outcomes for eating the produce: both allowed, both forbidden, only the seller allowed, or only the buyer allowed. The cases will be explained next.

steps.title: רבא explains the four cases of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא matches each of the four outcomes in רב ספרא's ברייתא to a specific wording of the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא explained: Both may eat when the seller says, 'Acquire as much as your money covers.' Both are forbidden when he says, 'When you bring the money, acquire from now.' The seller may eat and the buyer may not when he says, 'When you bring the money, acquire.' The buyer may eat and the seller may not when he says, 'Acquire from now, and my money will be a loan with you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא's ברייתא listed four outcomes without saying when each one applies. רבא fills in the missing detail by giving the exact wording of the sale for each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding question is who owns the field before the rest of the money is paid. Whoever clearly owns it may eat the produce. If the other side ate, he would be getting extra benefit because of money that is like a loan, and that is רבית. When ownership depends on something that has not happened yet, both sides are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: answered after him; explained the teaching right after it was said
acquire as much as your money covers; the buyer owns a share for each payment
when you bring the money
from now; ownership counts back to today
a loan

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up cases 2 and 3. Both say 'when you bring the money,' but only case 2 adds 'from now.' That one word makes ownership uncertain, so both sides are forbidden. Without it, the seller clearly owns the field until full payment, so only the buyer is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This lines up with steps 5–6. רב הונא, who says the seller eats, matches case 3. רב ענן matches case 2: both are forbidden, so the produce is set aside with a third party.

phrases.english: Rava answered after him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב ספרא, who just taught the ברייתא. רבא is explaining it.

phrases.english: Sometimes both of them are permitted,
where he said to him: Acquire according to the amount of your money.
Sometimes both of them are forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ: לְכִי מַיְיתֵית קְנִי מֵעַכְשָׁיו.
phrases.english: where he said to him: When you bring the money, acquire from now.
Sometimes the seller is permitted and the buyer is forbidden,
where he said to him: When you bring the money, acquire.
Sometimes the buyer is permitted and the seller is forbidden,
where he said to him: Acquire from now,
and my money will be a loan with you.
phrases.notes: "My money" means the amount the buyer still owes. The seller has turned it into a loan to the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains when each of the four outcomes in the ברייתא of step 7 applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case definition by the exact wording of the sale
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The four outcomes of the ברייתא seem to have no clear rule behind them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each outcome depends on the seller's wording, which decides who owns the field before full payment.

steps.title: Which תנא holds that both are forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion lies behind the case where both buyer and seller are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught that both of them are forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by asking which תנא would rule that both sides are forbidden in case 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In case 2 it is unknown whether eating would ever turn out to be רבית, since that depends on whether the money is paid later. Forbidding both sides is a strict ruling, so the גמרא wants to know who holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: who is the תנא (which sage) who taught this?

phrases.english: Who taught that both of them are forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of one ruling from רבא's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that uncertain רבית forbids both sides in case 2.

steps.title: Not רבי יהודה, who permits uncertain רבית
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the ruling is not like רבי יהודה, because רבי יהודה permits a case that might or might not become רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: It is not like רבי יהודה. For if it were רבי יהודה, he says that a case where only one possibility leads to רבית is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers the question. Whoever taught 'both are forbidden,' it cannot be רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In case 2 each side eats produce that may or may not turn out to be רבית, depending on what happens later. רבי יהודה permits that kind of uncertain רבית, so by his view eating would be allowed. The ruling 'both forbidden' must therefore come from the חכמים who disagree with him.

keyTerms.meaning: only one side of the possibilities leads to רבית; uncertain רבית
not in line with the opinion of
but he says! (points to a known opinion)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
It is not like Rabbi Yehuda.
For if it were Rabbi Yehuda, he says:
One side toward interest is permitted.
phrases.notes: He means a deal that will become רבית only if things go one particular way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling follows the חכמים against רבי יהודה, since רבי יהודה permits uncertain רבית.
steps.whatToRemember: Case 2 (both forbidden) assumes that uncertain רבית is forbidden. רבי יהודה disagrees and permits it.

steps.title: Making the borrower promise to sell the pledged property to the lender
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a lender may not make the borrower promise to sell him the pledged house or field at a fixed price, but he may at its market value.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a borrower pledged a house or a field to the lender, and the lender said, 'When you want to sell them, sell them only to me, at this price,' it is forbidden. If he said 'at their value,' it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a pledge that comes with a promise to sell. It forbids a fixed price and permits selling at the true value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fixed price would likely end up below the property's worth when it is sold, so the lender gains from the loan, which is רבית. At market value the lender gets no discount, only the right to buy first, and that is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: pledged as security for a loan
at this price; a fixed amount set now
at their value; the market price at the time of sale

phrases.aramaic: מִשְׁכֵּן לוֹ בַּיִת, מִשְׁכֵּן לוֹ שָׂדֶה,
phrases.english: If he pledged a house to him, or pledged a field to him,
and he said to him: When you want to sell them,
phrases.notes: Here the lender is speaking to the borrower.

phrases.english: you may sell them only to me
at this price, it is forbidden.
At their value, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁכֵּן לוֹ בַּיִת, מִשְׁכֵּן לוֹ שָׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: sale conditions linked to a loan with a pledge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A promise to sell the pledged property to the lender at a fixed price is forbidden as רבית. A promise to sell at market value is permitted.

steps.title: Who taught that 'at this price' is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind the ruling in the ברייתא from step 11 that a fixed-price promise is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught that saying 'at this price' is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion stands behind the ruling we just learned: a lender may not lock in a fixed price for the borrower's pledged field. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the ברייתא said a fixed price is forbidden, while market value is allowed. The fixed-price deal might or might not end up giving the lender extra value. So the גמרא wants to know which תנא forbids a deal whose interest is only possible, not certain.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the teacher (תנא) behind this ruling?
At this price: a price fixed ahead of time

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who taught that 'for this price' is forbidden?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא in step 11 about the lender and the pledged house or field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the ברייתא quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a fixed-price sale commitment from a borrower is forbidden as רבית.

steps.title: Not like רבי יהודה, who permits uncertain interest
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says this ruling does not follow רבי יהודה, since רבי יהודה permits a case of possible-but-not-certain interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: it is not like רבי יהודה. If it were רבי יהודה, he says that 'one side of רבית' (uncertain interest) is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers the question. This ruling is not רבי יהודה's view, because רבי יהודה allows deals that only might turn into interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fixed price may turn out to be a bargain for the lender, or it may not. That makes it 'one side of רבית': only a possible profit. רבי יהודה permits that, so a ruling that forbids it must come from the חכמים who argue with him.

keyTerms.meaning: A deal that only might end up as interest (uncertain interest)
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This same answer comes back in step 15, so it sets up the pattern for the next ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
for if it were Rabbi Yehuda, doesn't he say:
uncertain interest is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows the opinion against רבי יהודה, since רבי יהודה permits uncertain interest.

steps.title: Selling a field with a promise to sell it back
steps.stepSummary: A new ruling: if the seller says 'give it back when I have money,' the deal is forbidden. If the buyer says 'I'll give it back when you have money,' it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sold a house or a field and said, 'When I have money, return them to me,' it is forbidden. If the buyer says, 'When you have money, I will return them to you,' it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about a sale with a buy-back promise. Whether the deal is allowed depends on who makes the promise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the seller can always demand the field back, the 'sale' looks like a loan. The buyer eats the produce in the meantime, and that produce works like interest. When the buyer only volunteers to give it back, the sale is real, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: When I have money
Give them back to me
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The two cases sound almost identical. The only difference is who says the words: the seller (forbidden) or the buyer (permitted).

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר לוֹ בַּיִת, מָכַר לוֹ שָׂדֶה,
phrases.english: If he sold him a house, or sold him a field,
and said to him: 'When I have money,'
phrases.notes: Here the seller is the one speaking.

phrases.english: 'return them to me' – it is forbidden.
'When you have money,'
phrases.notes: Now the buyer is the one speaking.

phrases.english: 'I will return them to you' – it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָכַר לוֹ בַּיִת, מָכַר לוֹ שָׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new related ruling about sales that may hide a loan with interest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sale with a buy-back condition set by the seller is forbidden. A buy-back offered by the buyer is permitted.

steps.title: Same question and same answer: not like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who taught this ruling, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע again says it is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא? רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: it is not like רבי יהודה. If it were רבי יהודה, he says uncertain interest is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same 'who taught this?' question about the new ruling. It gets the same answer as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller might never get the money to buy the field back. In that case it was a real sale all along, and there was no interest. Since the interest is only possible, רבי יהודה would permit it, so the forbidding ruling cannot be his.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't he say? (a reminder of a known opinion)
For if
Not in accordance with

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who taught this?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.
For if it were Rabbi Yehuda, doesn't he say
uncertain interest is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same author question and answer from steps 12–13 to the ruling of step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא forbids the seller's buy-back condition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not רבי יהודה, since he permits uncertain interest.

steps.title: Why does the first case differ from the second?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the seller's version is forbidden while the buyer's version is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first case, and what is different about the last case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what really separates the two cases of step 14. This sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the field may go back to the seller once he has money. So the גמרא wants to know why the speaker's identity should change the law.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא?
phrases.english: What is different in the first clause, and what is different in the latter clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the distinction drawn in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the seller's condition is forbidden but the buyer's offer is permitted.

steps.title: רבא: it depends on whose free choice it is
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that in the first case the return was not left to the buyer's own choice, while in the second the buyer offered it by his own choice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: in the first case, he did not tell him it was of his own free will. In the last case, he told him it was of his own free will.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The difference is whether giving the field back is a condition forced on the buyer or a choice the buyer made himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller sets the condition, he can always pay and take the field back. So the deal is really a loan, and the produce the buyer eats is interest. If the buyer offers on his own, he could still choose to keep the field, so it is a real sale and the produce is truly his.

keyTerms.meaning: Of his own will / by his own choice

steps.whatToRemember: A buy-back the seller can demand turns a sale into a loan, so the buyer's produce is רבית. A buy-back the buyer offers freely leaves it a real sale.

phrases.english: Rava said: The first clause –
is where he did not tell him it would be of his own accord.
phrases.notes: Here the return is a condition the seller set, not something the buyer chose.

phrases.english: The latter clause – is where he said it to him of his own accord.
phrases.notes: The buyer volunteered the offer, so he can still decide to keep the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רֵישָׁא דְּלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ מִדַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by who controls the return of the field
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two cases seem the same, since in both the field may go back to the seller.
steps.terutzMaskana: A seller's condition makes it a loan with interest. A buyer's free offer keeps it a real sale.

steps.title: The seller who comforted the worried buyer
steps.stepSummary: A story: a man sold land without a guarantee, saw the buyer was upset, and promised to repay him with his best land plus improvements and produce if the land were seized.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man sold land to his friend without a guarantee. He saw that the buyer was sad, so he said to him: 'Why are you sad? If they take it away from you, I will pay you from the best land, plus the improvements and the produce.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a land sale. It sets up a question the גמרא will deal with next: whether this promise creates a problem of רבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sale was made with no guarantee, so the seller originally owed nothing if a creditor seized the field. Now he adds a promise to pay back the improvements and produce too. That extra payment is what may raise a רבית question.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantee to repay the buyer if the land is taken away
Sad, worried
They seized (a creditor took the land)
The best-quality land
Improvements, added value
Produce

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּזַבֵּין לֵיהּ אַרְעָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ
phrases.english: There was a certain man who sold land to his fellow
without a guarantee,
phrases.notes: If a creditor of the seller later took the land, the seller would not have to pay the buyer back.

phrases.english: He saw that he was distressed.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: He said to him: Why are you distressed?
If they seize it from you,
I will pay you from the best land, the improvement, and the produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּזַבֵּין לֵיהּ אַרְעָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ שֶׁלֹּא בְּאַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new practical case about land sales and possible רבית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a seller who sold without a guarantee later promises full repayment, including improvements and produce.

steps.title: אמימר begins his ruling on the seller's promise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces אמימר, who is about to give a ruling on the seller's promise from the previous story.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא introduces אמימר, who is about to explain the legal status of the seller's promise, and his actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18 the seller promised to repay the buyer with his best land, improvements and produce if the land were seized. That raises a question: is such a promise fully binding? This line opens אמימר's answer, but the content of the ruling has not appeared yet.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the ruling in this line. It only names who is speaking, and what he rules comes right after.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a ruling that deals with the legal status of the promise made in the Step 18 story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not stated yet. This line only introduces אמימר's upcoming ruling on the seller's promise.
